subject: Banking
title: Auto Loans: Dealership Kickbacks
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Auto Loans: Dealership Kickbacks.

hook.text: Car dealerships mark up your auto loan rate by 1-2% and keep the difference. The bank and dealer both profit from you.

buildup.text: The bank offers the dealer a rate of 5%. The dealer tells you the rate is 7%. That 2% markup is the dealer's commission.

discovery.text: US auto loan debt is $1.6 trillion. Banks earn interest while dealers earn markups. The borrower pays both.

twist.text: Getting pre-approved before visiting the dealer eliminates the markup. Most buyers don't know this simple trick.

climax.text: Auto lending shows how banking profits are shared with distribution partners. The dealer sells access to your wallet.

punchline.text: Dealer marks up your rate by 2%. Pre-approval saves you thousands.

quiz.question: How do car dealerships profit from auto loans?
options: They mark up the bank's rate and keep the difference

details.summary: Banks earn billions from auto loans, often paying dealers a markup for steering customers to higher interest rates than they qualify for. This dealer reserve system adds thousands of dollars to the cost of car financing.
details.whyItMatters: Most car buyers do not realize the dealership is profiting by inflating their interest rate. The dealer reserve system creates a hidden cost that falls disproportionately on less financially savvy borrowers.
takeaways: Dealers can mark up bank-approved interest rates by 1-3 percentage points
The dealer keeps the difference between the bank's rate and the customer's rate
Markup disparities have been found across racial demographics

faq.question: How does the dealer markup system work?
faq.answer: A bank might approve you for 5% interest, but the dealer offers 7% and keeps the 2% spread as profit. The bank benefits from a higher-rate loan, and the dealer earns a kickback, while the customer pays thousands more over the loan's life.

faq.question: How can car buyers avoid inflated interest rates?
faq.answer: Get pre-approved for an auto loan from your bank or credit union before visiting the dealership. This gives you a baseline rate to compare against the dealer's offer and eliminates the information asymmetry that dealers exploit.
